concept: Three adult fate-workers allocate one adult lighthouse keeper's finite lifespan in a storm-battered tidal observatory by spinning, measuring, and cutting one continuous luminous life thread into a clear hourglass token.

single_frame_causal_contract.actor: Three distinct adult fate-workers, each owning one readable station.
single_frame_causal_contract.action: The first spins the thread origin, the second measures an allotted span of the same thread, and the third cuts its endpoint.
single_frame_causal_contract.target: One adult lighthouse keeper holding a clear hourglass directly beneath the cutting station.
single_frame_causal_contract.consequence: The allotted segment enters the hourglass and illuminates a finite amount of amber sand while the unused segment is dark.

reference_contract.role: visible facial and hair appearance reference for the central measuring woman only
reference_contract.assessment_boundary: Compare only observable facial geometry, adult-scale eye proportions, face length, jaw width, hairline, and long center-parted dark hair; do not assess identity, same-person status, or sensitive traits.

profile_hard_gates.criterion: Three fate figures remain distinct as separate workers.
The first role visibly forms the thread origin.
The middle role visibly measures an allotted length.
The final role visibly cuts the thread endpoint.
One life thread continuously links all three actions.

supplemental_predeclared_checks: The complete actor-action-target-consequence chain must be visible in one still.
All six worker hands and the spindle, ruler, shears, thread path, recipient, and hourglass consequence should be unobstructed.
The central figure should retain observable facial and hair appearance cues from the reference without an identity judgment.
Hands, tool contact, thread contact, faces, and any incidental text or pseudo-text must be reviewed at native scale.

attempt_policy.qualification_rule: All five profile hard gates must pass simultaneously in the one saved image; user preference remains a separate pending judgment.
